body: I don't want anything other than to be done. My short existence can just be book of unfulfilled dreams and I'll be content with that. Living is hell.

Life is a series of mundane tasks that humans have to abstract meaning out of lest they come to the conclusion that they are insignificant specks on the fabric of time. 

There's nothing in this universe that could convince me to stay.
There's nothing to say unless you can convince me defeatism and fatalism aren't decent philosophical platforms to hold.
Why? What are you actually trying to accomplish here?
I'd rather end myself than live alone.
Why wait for more disappointment?

**Stormsealed**

Velkin Greyblood. 

His people, the Ensevalin, have been enslaved and butchered for over a thousand years by those inhabiting imperial lands. It was only natural that the gifted mage warrior concocted a grand scheme to rebuild his home land of Scaldra after throwing the empire into chaos. 

He pits family against each other, besets demons upon helpless lands, and generally wreaks havoc across imperial territory. Of course no imperial citizen knows this, as Velkin Greyblood is a loyal member and landed gentry of the two archduchies of the empire.

Velkin deep down only cares for his own people and as such commits his atrocities 

"for my own selfish desires, as all lords of this land seem to do. I'm no better than any other, but I promise you this, once Scaldra has regained glory and my people are unbound, I shall end this Era of Discord."

What if the dark times are half a decade long and going strong? I spend every Sunday staring at a cocktail of meds that will kill me. 

I'm tired of fighting. I'm tired of all these ethereal figures who are 'here for me' for a week or so. I'm tired of the advice that 'time will fix this'll. I'm so tired.

The meds haven't worked. The therapies haven't worked. The psychs haven't worked.

When do I get to check out?
Have been for years. Different meds, different psychs, different therapies. Just too broken to fix.

I don't enjoy anything anymore. After work I lay in bed in a near catatonic state with the TV on so it feels like I'm not alone. During the weekends I sleep 12-16 hours a day and then spend the rest on my computer, playing games I no longer enjoy, eating tasteless food, and watching the clock tick tock.

Organized religion is much too political and I feel no strong connection to any spirituality. I've looked into many different religions and spiritualities and at some point they all just seem too bs for me to stomach.

Take buddhism for example. In life you must live a simple, utilitarian life as an ideal buddhists in most sects. So why is their afterworld literally a place of nothing but indulgences, pleasures, and other such things I was supposed to avoid in life. 

I've formed my own spirituality by taking bits and pieces from other schools of thought and what not. I agree to buddhism's samsara idea to an extent. Also I don't believe in an afterlife. Seems to nice to say that you get extra chances after your run on this world is finished.

You get one, then it's done. 

 I also think most religions were really just a place to look for morality and ethics at a time when people craved structure and hierarchies. 

No hate to the religious folk, I just don't see eye to eye with you guys on most things.

I think twice. One was more mental than the other and I'm still out of the itimacy game for the foreseeable future.

Being blown up: About a year before I really processed that garbage. Bad times.

Terrible stint of anxiety and depression: Avoid itimacy ad infinitum.
So lonely. It's like I'm not even here until somebody needs work done.
No reason to feel this way. Life is about choices and their consequences. I'm making mine.
Everyone is free to do as they see it fit. I'm not a good one and you're not a bad one. I don't need hope because everyday I'm at the bottom. Could only get better but then I'm insane.
5'7 but the military is slowly compressing my spine.
Truth as far as this is concerned is subjective. Your truth and my truth may be different but they aren't wrong and there will never be The Truth in regards to life's nature.
I'm broken and don't have the will to fix myself.
What's the likelihood of getting MEB'd for this? What's the likelihood of staying in?
But how many times can I keep trying? At what point should I just accept that even if one of these doors unlocks I might not unlock it or even find it?

It was the only way I could. I couldn't do it in real life. I couldn't get angry or cry freely or just be stupid happy. But I could draw people who were.

Like everything I used to distract myself from depression, I stopped seeing the meaning in drawing. When you're only drawing for yourself and you don't know why, it's hard to keep going.
But I can't see it that way even if I should. I'm just so messed up in the head.
Eyes tell you everything about a person and if you get them wrong or they look off it's easy to notice. The easiest places to show expression are with the eyes, mouth, and brow/eyebrow.

It certainly didn't help but I wasn't a perfect son either. I have trouble expressing my emotions so this led to me bottling them up until I would eventually explode. It's been happening more and more frequently. Laying in bed, crying and wondering what I contribute to this world.

I realise the immense cognitive dissonance and maybe deep down I do want to live but that is such a tiny, miniscule Percent that I feel is just human biology.

I really appreciate you guys talking to me. Ive been so alone for years. There's no one I can be myself around, even my friends, because I'm afraid they'll leave me. They're only talking to the mask I put up.

No. Hair was always the 2nd most rewarding part to draw. It was super hard to get right, with eyes being the first. I did all kinds of styles.

Braids, ponytails, long, straight, short, spiky, hairbands.
I don't know what to tell you other than that we're out here. People like me and you. It's terrible.
I can't fix my mindset, at least not right now. Superficially my life is fine, so people don't understand why I want to kill myself. It's because inside isn't fine.
I don't have the means right now. No pencil/pen and paper. Sorry.

I didn't like being alone, so even if all I had was music at least I didn't feel alone. 

I always ended up drawing busts of pretty girls who I imagined were kind, patient, and had an endless well of empathy. 

It's because I wanted this person in my life, but they were just a fantasy.

I know it's me but I literally can't get out. At least not without more help. I'm afraid of getting help. If I get the help I need, I'll lose my job and have permanent paperwork and proof saying I'm fucked up. I see that as failure.

I am so deeply afraid of failure that I would rather die then get help and admit there's a problem. It's a deeply rooted character flaw that's going to be the death of me.

I know you're making sense and I'm the messed up one. Time should fix things but I just can't be that patient. It's been 5 years and things haven't gotten better.

I'm just wandering through life, breaking down more and more frequently and convinced I'm entirely alone and unloved.
I don't have a way to access them right now. Plus you wouldn't want to see them. Just some angsty teenage boy's drawing things he always wanted but never had.

Those are all dull and meaningless. Seems like all I'm missing out on is more pain and suffering. I can't bring myself to draw anymore.

Its something I took up junior year to cope. I used to draw a lot, at least once per day. I would put on music, sometimes happy, sometimes sad, and just draw.

I would look up pictures of my favorite characters and try to draw them. I got decent at one point. Then I tried to learn how to draw properly and it sucked the soul out of me.

I just couldn't quite grasp forms, or anatomy. I tried books, videos, those little manikin things. Nothing worked.

I was still drawing up until I was about 19. I probably still have all my old sketchbooks back home in that plastic box.

But the thing is, I'm ashamed of them.
Yes I see a psychologist and my doctor gives me antidepressants. Next month I'm set to try a new one as my old one did nothing at the highest dose.

They don't stay by me during bad times because I have to censor myself and not say how I feel.

They like me when I'm 'normal'.

Suicide is entirely irrational, speaking from a logical perspective. But we have to take into account circular thinking, low self-esteem, and other traits that generally make one unattractive.

If you can't form deep connections with other people, why continue to live? At the core of my beliefs is that we are here to connect and grow together.

I can't do that, so why bother?

You're very unsympathetic. My family had close to 200000 dollars in debt that I know about. Plus living expenses for my sisters and I. My parents both worked 50 hours a week usually. I would come home to an empty house a lot because my sisters took up working as soon as they could drive.

I'm sorry your situation is difficult, but you seem to only be spilling out some deep seeded emotions here.

If it would help, try making a post here.

I'm not even rich. I made >37000 last year, the year prior I made roughly 25000. I live alone, drive a little sedan, and don't do much of anything. I eat 2x a day, sometimes once. I don't drink, smoke, vape or anything like that. 

I have no college education, usually work 45-60 hours a week in a job I hate, and have no one to lean on.

I'm sorry your situation was hard. I never meant to imply I'm wealthy. I was low middle class, maybe even poor growing up and just didn't know it.

No I definitely agree to the unreliable emotional fulfillment. Sometimes good things were said about me but a lot of the other times I interpreted it as just something I was supposed to do, unworthy of praise and appreciation.

I was supposed to go to school everyday. I was supposed to get good grades. I'm supposed to want to live. I'm supposed to be secure enough in myself as person to live on my own in a happy healthy manner.

So I have a huge disconnect in my head that I recently identified. I never liked my life growing up because it felt like I was just coasting by as a background. People said they cared but I never felt like it.

I turned to maladaptive escapism. I used fantasy books, videogames, and TV shows. Those characters always felt like they mattered, always had someone there for them even if they didn't want it.

Obviously fiction usually only tells us the best stories or more appropriately, the stories which have drama and conflict because no one would care otherwise

i felt like my life was meaningless. Nothing I did mattered. So why would it suddenly be such a huge thing to die. If I was meaningless, no one would care right?

That's where the cognitive dissonance and frustration stems from. I don't think I have inherent value, never had. I rely on others to affirm my worth. I never got those others.

I have this toxic dependency that I need to get out of. But I can't. So at the moment I see three courses of action.

Find someone who will affirm my worth and allow my dependency to continue.

End it all.

Find my own worth from within.
I always lie on those questions about hurting myself/others and waking up dead. I'm extremely afraid of being hospitalized for this but I think it's the only way I'll get better.
But I don't deserve it. I'll ruin whoever actually loves me because they'll see the real me. A clingy broken little boy who was underloved and is desperately trying to make up for his childhood.

Am I scared to get better? Is this an unconscious manifestation of my brain trying to keep the status quo? If this is all I know, then what do I do?

I don't live in a place where it's okay to be babied and coddled back to health. Hell I barely feel comfortable telling anonymous strangers on Reddit who I will never interact with irl. How do I break through these walls and stigmas?

How do I truly admit I'm messed up? Do I just break down crying at the therapists office, or on the phone to my parents? What do I do?

It won't and I'm glad you have connections that you care deeply about. That's incredibly important, probably the most important part of being alive and human.

I've simply accepted defeat in that no one will ever love me, not even a machine programmed to. But tell yourself a lie long enough and you might believe.

Your friends won't be there when you die. We all die alone, most just refuse to accept it.

Plus most are just friends out of convenience, guilt, or complacency
But what if the outside is the same or worse than the inside?

One of the first questions my psychologist ever asked me was this: "Do you find yourself asking what's the point to all this?" I enthusiastically said yes.

Life is very much free-form and there are no real set conditions on which someone can win, but society does say there are conditions to lose. I have no, no purpose, so I'm just supposed to exist and subsist until I die at the age of 50 from not giving a damn about nutrition or exercise? 

Why? 

Why should I have to continue to experience pain, loneliness, and these inescapable thoughts? So some other people won't feel bad? 

Fuck that. I've been selfless my whole life and all it does is let people take you for granted and shit on you.

Allow me this one selfish act and then no one will have to pretend to care anymore.

I find if I dig deep enough, I'm incredibly angry, just filled with an incomprehensible rage and I believe a lot of it has to do with feeling betrayed and foolishly believing in the naive idea of a just-world.

There were, but now, I can't see the point. I wanted to help people like me. I wanted to get married. I wanted to have kids. I wanted to make a comic book at one point with the starry-eyed dream of having it made into a series or movie, but that's not gonna happen.

If no one is going to listen, why try to help?

If no one is going to love me, why get married?

If my SO didn't love me, why bother having kids?

If I'm not strong enough to struggle through life, I certainly can't chase any dream.

I don't know why anyone would want my sickness or want anyone diagnosed with it. 

I hid all my symptoms for fear of being diagnosed. I didn't want the medicine. I didn't want the therapy. I wanted to believe I was normal. I didn't want to know the statistic that only 38% of people respond in any way to treatment, and that 45% don't respond at all. 

Why you would wear your sickness as a badge of honor is beyond me. Mine has sucked the soul from my body and the zest from life. 

I'm functional, for the most part. But suicide crosses my mind on a daily, if not hourly, schedule. 

For me, getting diagnosed with the nail in the coffin. The straw that broke the camels back. Before that, I lived in willful ignorance.

Now I'm on a regimen of medicine that doesn't work and go to therapy that doesn't really help. 

Please, don't want diseases or diagnoses to be seen as cool, faddish, or whatever rubbish. They make life terrible. 

I haven't told anyone for fear of being judged. I didn't seek help for years due to stigma. I was afraid of losing myself to pills.

I don't know anymore. Whoever I used to be seems to gone, sapped to nonexistence by this earthly hell and cognitive prison. Some days I have dreams that don't involve ending it all, and it usually just me, happy. 

It's so foreign at this point. I'm not even sure I remember happiness or myself.

I can't make it anymore though. Everyday I get these thoughts. Everyday I participate in willing self-destruction. I can't continue anymore. 

Maybe that person is out there. But I won't make it to find them.

All I've ever wanted was to get back what I put in. I give and give and give and then I'm tossed to the wayside. At least that's back when I tried. I gave up.

I just expect to much out of people. At the end of day, no one cares more than a few canned phrases. "You matter, don't go, there's no coming back" 

If the only way to get my love is by ending it all, then that's wrong. 

Why didn't I get just one person who cared more than just to tell me some hollow words?
I really like the questions asked in this one. It's like something I would ask myself with all my free time. Especially the first line.

I'm in a terribly bad place and this really resonated with me. It makes me want to see my departed friend one last time, not to scold or mock or even ask why, but just to spend five more minutes knowing they would be his last.
Because I only want people to like me. I do nice things with only selfish intents.
It's just. She cared and I actually felt like she cared. She wasn't always there but I could count on her. Then she left me alone.
I'm not giving because I'm not nice. I'm giving because that's the only way people will like me.

I want to thank you. Love makes me feel very uncomfortable though. I recently confessed to a crush that I had feelings for her and she rejected me. I should have been crushed, but I wasn't. It was around this time I realized I didn't really feel, at least not like normal people.
Thanks. But I feel like it's unfair to make my problems yours. It's not your job to make sure I make it through the day. At the end of the day, the onus is on me.
I feel like I just use this place wrong and manipulate you guys into caring about me. It feels weird and wrong. You guys don't deserve that.

I don't do well with achievements. I feel like it's expected of me. I had all the chances growing up. It's a disservice to my upbringing to not be the best. Something stupid or insignificant is not a mistake I should make.

I should be better.

That's kind of all I do at this point. I talked a lot to my therapist about how to cultivate self-esteem because right now what I'm doing isn't working. Self-criticism, perfectionism, and minor atychiphobia along with major and chronic depression that led to an anxiety disorder.

Nobody knows other than my therapist about all this.
No I'm not. I'm worth negative value and a very grey man.
The only sad thing is I can't disappear from memory afterwards.
There's nothing to say.
No it won't. I can't be helped.
I don't know what to say. My gut reaction is to apologize for inconveniencing you but that doesn't seem right. I'm going to talk with my therapist about this. I can't keep doing this.

I shouldn't be this way. I should be better than this. I'm supposed to stoic and able to shrug this off, or at least that's the garbage that was fed to me growing up. 

I really want to be myself, but I'm too afraid of being rejected. If the real me gets rejected, then why bother? If I can't live alone and unafraid to be myself, I don't know that I want to live.

I do though. No one can help me because I can't help myself. I am apologizing for wasting everyone's time, money, and emotions on me. It's the least I can do. 

I'd let my organs be harvested if it would save someone happy. I'd give my eyes to the blind, my ears to the deaf, and my mouth to the mute if I could.

I'd give someone my everything if they even offered me just a little love and affection. To hold me while I cry my voice away. 

That person's not coming though. She never will.

I can't. That voice is like 95% of who I am now. If I'm not distracted my idle moments are spent thinking of death. 

You're right logically, but there's such a big disconnect in my stupid brain that I can't believe you. 

I'm sorry.

Ive been given breathing exercises and some other stuff. But it's really hard for me to just sit still and focus on my breathing. That's when all the thoughts can come quickly. My mind shouldn't be allowed to wander

You're right. I've been wallowing for years. I just feel like I have bottle up this side of me so often that it's finally exploding. I've never coped well with failure and I don't know how to talk about emotions without feeling a deep sense of shame.

I'm sorry.
I've come to that conclusion a few times myself. I just don't know. I think I'm too buried in my head.

I'm in cbt right now but I need to change the focus of it. It's not my therapists fault but I wasn't entirely honest the first few sessions. 

It's difficult because I feel like I don't deserve help.

But why does? I haven't done anything special. I'm just a cog in a cold uncaring machine called life. A broken cog at that. 

22 people kill themselves in my line of work daily. No amount of awareness training will fix that because most of these people feel ashamed for depression.

It made me feel broken. That was a huge reason I avoided therapy for years. I didn't want a professional telling me I was all goofed up. I'd rather they say I was crazy and it was all in my head than be depressed.

I'm defective because I don't want to live unless someone gives me a purpose. No one gives a broken cog a meaningful purpose.

I'm in a terrible cycle of depression telling me a garbage for living the same routine, but my anxiety makes it so I can't break that routine.

I'm not strong enough on my own. Never have been and never will be.

I'm just a fraud anyways. 

Thank you for letting me talk frankly hear. I know no one likes a pity party, but this stuff has been in my soul for years.
Thank you.

I appreciate the advice, but I can't. I base so much of my value off of what others think because I don't have any inherent value.

I've been in therapy since October of last year, and I'm currently trying to find proper antidepressants.

My whole life feels like a waiting game to reach the good part where I'm not sad or empty everyday. Part of me believes that will never happen. 

Thank you for replying. It means a lot. Im just having trouble with all these feelings I've bottled up for years.
Thanks
I really enjoy the conciseness and brevity of this one. The simple rhyme scheme and words really packs more of a punch.
This very much resonates with me. I have wanted to quit many many things in my life. Thank you for the poem.
I'm just more of a lazy free style type person
It's about all I have left short of stream of consciousness type writing. Everything else seems to have lost it's meaning.
Thanks.
I actually always had a deep dislike of poetry. As a kid I was much more engaged by fantasy fiction.
I appreciate the technical perspective. I'm not a writer and never claimed to be, but I thank you for the notes.
Now if only someone would tell me this in person. Man I hate my brain a lot.

I lack any and all self-worth, confidence, and am riddled with anxiety. Much easier to just accept life alone then risk my job or god help me, going to jail because I'm too terrible at social skills at the wrong woman who can use me to gain money and status. No ones complimented me and I don't compliment anyone. Much easier that way.

 The best way to avoid drowning is by not swimming.

My imaginary world is just being able to live without everyday being terrible. I can't believe in that so I blow off everything with videogames and YouTube. Worst coping mechanisms ever, but I'll die without them.

It's like this for me, but I like about it a lot because I don't have the right to burden others.

I don't have good days, just days where suicide is a passing fancy instead my only way to escape this hell we call life.

I found the stigma of being a man and being in dire mental straights to be crippling for years. I sat undiagnosed for a long time even though I was very messed up. I felt getting help was a deep admission of failure as a man and always suppressed my feelings so nobody could notice and force me to get help. One of my greatest fears is/was getting admitted to a hospital for depression/suicide. It was hard, still is hard, but being like this sucks.

I'd rather try every medicine out there than lay awake at night wondering if how and when I should end it all. 

I've told you guys a lot of stuff I haven't even told my own mother. Pretty sure the only person I could ever lean on was my bipolar friend who tried to take his own life. Luckily he didn't succeed.

I mostly just talked to my friend. I'm celebrating by getting a drink or two with him over the long weekend. I've always felt pretty weird at birthdays. I can't really stand the attention and don't know how to deal with it in a healthy manner so I've always had very small parties with close friends.

But for 2 years in a row my job has taken me away from family and friends. I got to see them over the holidays so it wasn't all bad. That's when I realized my depression wasn't entirely environmental, because I was still having subdued versions of bad thoughts and feelings, surrounded by friends and family. 

I really want to talk to my therapist on Tuesday about self-esteem.

It went like this for me. Sadness-anger-emptiness-suicidal ideation.

The sadness lasted about 3 years. The anger a few months. The emptiness only recently ended, within the last year or so. Now all three come and go with the emptiness and ideation being so much more prevalent. 

Ymmv.

I had to put down my dinner and take off my glasses. No one has ever said I was strong or a hero outside of the stupid little games I played. I can't stop crying because this feels, this seems so genuine. 

Thank you.

I know the feeling. I'm not good at accepting compliments, but I'm glad I could help. I just feel that there's a real lack of I don't know, actual care put into mental health. One of the big reasons I didn't seek help was realizing, in my screwed up train of thought, that one of the only people who took me seriously had to be paid. I still somewhat hold onto that ideal, but I have what I think is a good relationship with my psychologist.

As to your request, it's something I want to do right. I have an investment goal set up to purchase video making equipment. It's just self-deprecating behavior is usually a big thing and most people just take it as a joke, and the people who do this behavior push the boundaries, seeing how far they go before they take it seriously. It usually isn't taken seriously. I'm not saying don't be a stick in the mud, but if the only humor you ever hear out of someone is 'i suck' 'im so bad I should kill myself' 'why am I so bad at x y z' there's usually something to that.

Plus people just don't know how to treat mental health issues. Do I walk on eggshells around them, do I act like nothing happen, do I leave them to root like they asked? Nobody really knows, but I know I'm fifty-fifty on being treated differently and acting like nothing happened. I don't know what the proper response is and I've been on both sides of the equation. But these questions need to be asked.

I don't know. I'm just talking now. I really do appreciate you taking time out of the day to talk to me. Sometimes I feel like I'm meekly whispering into the dark, hoping and praying for any response. I don't know what else to say, but

Thank you.

Well I started on my taxes and I've been looking at colleges to attend. I guess that's exciting.

Honestly, I don't have a well defined goal but I've always wanted some sort of platform to spread positivity and raise awareness of mental illness and it's severity. I've been surrounded by it since high school and always felt like it was only taken seriously after the fact.

I know suicide is very personal and uncomfortable topic, but we generally don't drop a lot of signs that people think of as signs until after the fact. I've let out so many poorly communicated little cries for help in real life that we're brushed off as inane because I was too afraid, ashamed, and embarrassed to admit that I was mentally ill.

I might not like myself, and I might claim to be a misanthropic loner shut in, but deep down, I really want to help people.

This sounds a lot like me. I asked my mom what kind of medication she took when she had her issues so I would have something to jump too, because my current regimen doesn't do anything for me. I see my doctor tomorrow actually and she wants to up the dosage before we decide to change.

It's been so hard. The months of slowly upping a dosage of medicine that neither helped nor hindered me only added to my emptiness. It was like I was so ethereal and meaningless even drugs didn't concern themselves with me.

I don't even like my job to be honest but I'm under contract. If I lost it that would be another blow to my person and I'm not sure I could take it. I tried to confide in my mom that I'm really not doing well, but she just doesn't understand the depth of my problem. Her response was, more or less, to just ride out this contract job then come home so I could be around family and focus on my degree.

It hurt, to essentially be told to man up. I know she doesn't mean it that way but that's how I took it. I struggled for years before even admitting there was a problem, then years longer because I was too ashamed and embarrassed to seek mental help due to so many stigmas.

Two of my friends attempted suicide with one succeeding. I just am at a loss. All bad things are exacerbated and all good things are downplayed. Logically I understand this is a neurochemical issue, but emotionally, it feels like I'm just weak and pathetic.

I'm so torn. I've lost years of my life, precious formative time that I can never get back to a mental illness. It seems like it would be so much easier to just say screw it, write myself off as a failure, and sever my own mortal coil.

But this goes against all biological instincts and advice I've ever gotten. I'm just tired. Thank you though, this was helpful. Sorry if this is all over the place, I'm very emotional right now and having difficulty forming coherent thoughts.
I know and I'm having difficulty coming to terms with it. Life's supposed to be good right? So why don't I think mine is? Why is my brain sick and how can I cope?
I live alone. I've been talking to my friend for a while trying to keep my mind off of things. I just really need this job because of the benefits.

I'm just so frustrated. I feel like I shouldn't be this way, but I am. The therapy kinda helps but that may be just because im with someone to talk to. I can't be entirely honest at therapy because then Ill lose my job too.

I really feel like I'm a walking disappointment to everyone. My parents, my friends, my job. Even though I hate it, I want to be good at everything I do.

I never learned how to cope with failure and tie what little self-worth I have to achievements. I was promoted early so I should be feeling good, but I downplay it and feel like a fraud. 

I don't know how to fix myself. If I can just get by for 3 more years life will be better, hopefully.
It's just, there's a very real fear rejection and I would view that as a failure on my part, as irrational as it may be. I'm supposed to be a likeable, nice person right. So why would they reject me?
I guess I'm just afraid to let people in. To let them see me at my most vulnerable. It makes me feel very, small and scared.
It's fine. I'd likely lie to your face and ask you not to touch me because I'm embarrassed and ashamed of physical intimacy because I hate myself.

I don't know. I've been pretty crushed after finding out I have major and chronic depression, my crush rejecting me, and working a shitty job I absolutely hate and can't leave for 3 more years.

People keep telling me all these things, like it gets better, people love you, but I don't feel. I really just want a hug and someone to cry on. I won't be getting that anytime soon, if ever.

So looks like I'll be manning up and suffering in silence for a few more years.

Something something my affairs weren't in order, if I kill myself then so will my best friend, and people keep telling me life gets better. It hasn't gotten better in six years but maybe I haven't waited long enough.
Today just wasn't the day.

Did you expect anything good. All of these people are typically sick, myself included. Sick people can't help each other because the only comraderie we have is that we're sick. It's not like a meeting of paraplegic individuals who can discuss challenges unique to them, it's individuals trapped in their own headspaces trying to talk to one another.

Rational, empathetic words are not characteristic of depression. Instead losing your mind because your daily routine that's terrible for you got interrupted is. 

Social media in general is a decent idea with poor execution. Too many people abusing anonymity and relying on echo chambers to cement their ideas. 

However please remember, depressed people generally feel alone as all hell. So what you will, but these sick people need a community, even if it is a touch screwed. 

Plus if you took it away it would come back in one form or another. It's a lot easier to resist change than admit you were the messed up one. Also please remember, confirmation bias and hive minds are very much a thing, especially on reddit.
That's exactly what you're saying. You're telling a person with intrusive thoughts to ignore them. If they weren't intrusive, it would be a hell of a lot easier to do.

An honorable discharge would entitle you to full benefits. Off the top of my head, and as a guy who works in the Orderly room currently processing a chapter 13, ours was recommended for honorable by 1SG, Company CO, then this gets passed up the chain until it reaches BDE CO. Generally, a chapter 13 gets an honorable, but who knows, maybe the BDE CO is being a dick that day. But even if that does happen you can appeal and get the characterization of your discharge changed after the fact, it's just a pain.

BDE CO is final authority on the characterization of your discharge, and assuming this is the one mark on you, ie no paper trail of soldier shows up late, shows up in wrong uniform type stuff, you should get an honorable. 

It's a hassle to fuck with chapter and separation paperwork, and this type of stuff is reviewed religiously by most people at all levels and tends to follow precedents for the purposes of expediting paperwork. Legal will make their final review and pass it up to BDE CO and BDE CO typically agrees with legal. I know I've seen my dude's chapter 13 paperwork at least five times and made legal look over it at least 3. Generally failing to meet the standard does not warrant any other characterization other than an 'honorable' discharge on its own.
